items.text: Proceed with a right-click menu to pop up speaker characterization instead of adding a button in the transcription box.
Implement a right-click menu option that displays speaker characterization when a user clicks on a speaker ID in the transcription box.
Include an option in the right-click menu to show all meetings a user has participated in.
Delay full integration of speaker characterization into browsing functionality until the core feature is implemented.
Explore linking speaker characterization with dialogue acts to improve browsing and topic navigation.
Prioritize defining the behavior of clicking on a user or topic before expanding speaker characterization features.
Include a search function to find meetings by user or topic in the browser interface.
Ensure speaker characterization is available as a feature, even if its utility is not yet fully defined.
Evaluate whether speaker characterization should be tied to topic-based filtering in the future.
Confirm that the right-click menu is a more intuitive and user-friendly option than relying on right-click behavior alone.
Consider adding a button alongside the summarization feature to trigger speaker characterization, as a fallback or alternative.
What is the user's intended use case for speaker characterization? How will it enhance browsing or topic navigation?
Double-clicking on a topic should open all meetings containing that topic by default, as it would save users from having to right-click and select an option.
The interface should allow users to toggle between transcription and summary views within a single window using buttons or checkmarks, rather than opening separate windows.
Right-click menus should be implemented for topics and user interactions to allow users to view meetings containing a specific topic or action.
Check the current behavior of double-click actions on topics or meetings to determine if they trigger any default behavior.
Evaluate whether single-channel audio files should be integrated into the system for use in transcription or analysis.
Assess the feasibility of implementing tabs in the interface to manage multiple views (e.g., transcription and summary) within one window.
Explore whether the current Java windowing toolkit supports tabbed interfaces or toggle buttons for switching between views.
Determine if there is a common default action for double-clicking (e.g., showing speaker characterization) that could be implemented as a default behavior.
Evaluate whether multiple windows (e.g., summary, transcription, topic lists) will cause clutter and consider minimizing window count.
What is the most common action users expect when double-clicking on a topic or meeting?
Should single-channel audio files be included in the system, or will they increase data footprint without sufficient benefit?
Will users typically have five or more windows open simultaneously, or will they mostly use two or three at a time?
The team agrees to provide three transcript alternatives: full meeting transcript, meeting transcript without disfluencies, and summaries.

The team will evaluate whether to include disfluency in the final transcript, with the option to provide both versions (with and without disfluencies).
The team agrees that the prototype should be completed by the end of February.
How much work is required to extract data from XML files for indexing, and what level of file manipulation is needed?

What is the current status of file access permissions for the GUI code directory?
Improving the user experience by reducing the number of open windows in Photoshop and similar tools.

The team agrees to share as much as possible when collaborating on projects, especially when starting new work.
The team decides to work on the weekend to begin developing features that can be integrated into the GUI by next week.
The team agrees that the current codebase contains a lot of unnecessary functions and will be cleaned up gradually.

Research query language capabilities to inform search design.

Schedule a meeting next week to review progress and show existing work.
